subject.title: fix(sqlite): allow verified shared wal backports

question: Should OpenClaw support a self-attested environment-variable bypass for shared-library SQLite backports, or require a stronger verifiable and auditable safety contract?
rationale: The implementation changes the corruption-safety boundary rather than merely correcting version parsing; source inspection cannot establish the project’s acceptable operator-trust model.

options.title: Keep the guard fail-closed
options.body: Do not merge a generic bypass until OpenClaw can support a stronger verification and support contract for distro backports.

options.title: Support an explicit escape hatch
options.body: Accept the self-attested environment variable as a documented operator-risk decision and add focused upgrade and deployment proof.

options.title: Define a verified backport mechanism
options.body: Design a platform/package-specific verification path before permitting known supported backports.

recommendation.title: Keep the guard fail-closed
recommendation.body: Do not merge a generic bypass until OpenClaw can support a stronger verification and support contract for distro backports.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged adjacent work owns the current SQLite safety diagnostic surface affected by this decision.
